__comment: Logweir v0.1. Every panel below reads ONLY a metric name crates/logweir/src/metrics.rs actually writes, and crates/logweir/tests/orchestrator.rs::the_textfile_metrics_carry_every_name_the_dashboard_reads asserts that every one of those names is emitted. If a panel is added here, add its metric there in the same commit — otherwise this repository ships a dashboard over a metric nothing writes. v0.1 has NO HTTP surface: the CLI writes a Prometheus TEXTFILE at --metrics-file and node_exporter's textfile collector scrapes it. `triggered_by` is deliberately NOT a label (unbounded cardinality) and lives in the scorecard, and so does `run_id`, which rides the textfile as a leading `# logweir run_id=` COMMENT line. ONE CARVE-OUT: the freshness panel "Time since the last drill reported" reads node_exporter's own node_textfile_mtime_seconds, not a Logweir series, and deliberately so — a metric Logweir writes cannot report that Logweir did not run, and that series carries no cluster label, so absence detection works identically on the terminal paths where the cluster id was never learned. Every OTHER panel still reads only a name crates/logweir/src/metrics.rs writes.
title: Logweir — restore drills

panels.title: Exit code of the last drill
panels.description: 0 pass. 1 operational — NO scorecard was written. 2 a drill result that is NOT a pass — a scorecard WAS written and signed; this is the most valuable result the tool produces and must not be confused with 1. 3 refused by a guard before anything ran. 4 signing or lock proof failed and nothing was uploaded.

panels.title: Drill runs by outcome
panels.description: logweir_drill_runs_total is a counter written once per run, labelled by outcome.

panels.title: Objectives met
panels.description: 1 met, 0 missed, per objective. ABSENT means the objective was not measurable — which is not the same as met, and is why this panel shows no value rather than a zero.

panels.title: RTO (seconds)
panels.description: logweir_drill_rto_seconds is measured.rto_excluding_preflight_seconds — the figure compared against objectives.rto_seconds, because header_preflight: full is a full read and decode of the window that no incident responder performs. The scorecard carries three other RTO figures; this is the one the objective is scored on.

panels.title: RPO (seconds)
panels.description: Archive COVERAGE GAP at the requested recovery point. This is NOT source-relative data loss: it says how far the archive's coverage falls short of the point you asked to recover to, not how many records the source held that the archive did not.

panels.title: Records that did not reconcile
panels.description: Per-record byte-fingerprint mismatches within the sampled window. A compacted target topic is reported through this path too, as a mismatch rather than as `partial` — see docs/stability.md.

panels.title: Integrity level achieved
panels.description: byte-fingerprint is the full per-record check. consume-only is the degraded level taken when the engine cannot supply what a fingerprint needs. not-attempted means no integrity check ran at all — read it as an absence of evidence, never as a pass.

panels.title: Integrity result
panels.description: pass, fail, or partial. A `partial` carries a partial_reason in the signed scorecard, which this dashboard cannot show — read the document.

panels.title: Evidence object lock verified
panels.description: 1 ONLY after a provider readback actually answered. object_store 0.14 models no Object Lock / WORM API on any backend Logweir can build, so this reads 0 on every backend today. 0 means NO PROOF WAS OBTAINABLE — it is not a finding that your bucket is unprotected.

panels.title: Scorecard fields redacted
panels.description: Fields removed from the scorecard before signing. 0 is the whole document every v0.1 run writes — v0.1 has no writer that can produce a redaction, so ANY non-zero value means the document was edited after signing-time construction or came from a reader-incompatible producer, and BOTH verifiers refuse it (`logweir drill verify` exit 4, docs/verify_scorecard.py exit 1). The series is emitted unconditionally, so `logweir_drill_redactions > 0` is a valid alert — an absent series and a whole document are otherwise indistinguishable to PromQL. The removed PATHS are deliberately not labels (unbounded cardinality); read them from `drill show`'s qualifiers footer or the notification body.

panels.title: Time since the last drill reported
panels.description: Seconds since the metrics file was last written, from node_exporter's own file mtime rather than from anything Logweir emits — a metric Logweir writes cannot report that Logweir did not run. Red past 8 days, which is the same threshold as the documented alert `time() - node_textfile_mtime_seconds{file=~".*logweir.*"} > 8d` (see docs/metrics.md). Every terminal path writes the file, so a value that stops advancing means the drill did not run or did not finish — not that it failed.

defaults.noValue: no textfile has ever been scraped — either no drill has run or --metrics-file is not mounted

panels.title: Last drill run (wall clock)
panels.description: The wall-clock second at which the last drill run ended and wrote this file. Emitted on EVERY terminal path, including the ones that produce no scorecard, so it answers "when did anything last happen" rather than "when did anything last pass". On a path that never reached the target cluster the label reads `unknown`.

panels.title: Scratch topics teardown left behind
panels.description: Scratch topics phase 9 created on the target cluster and could not delete, because the broker refused. Emitted on every scorecard-carrying path, 0 included, so 0 means phase 9 ran and cleaned up and only the absence of the whole textfile means no drill result was produced. A non-zero value does NOT mean the drill failed: the restore is verified and signed before phase 9 runs, so a run that leaves topics behind still exits 0. The topic names are on the run's WARN line and in the signed teardown attestation; they are deliberately not a label here, because topic names are cluster-controlled text and would be unbounded cardinality.
